summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and GJ tube dependence was admitted after transfer for a malfunctioning feeding tube that was displaced and likely caused aspiration pneumonia. He was stabilized, and a new GJ tube was successfully placed via interventional radiology. Nutrition was resumed, resolving mild hypoglycemia, and all chronic medications, including antiretrovirals, were restarted through the tube. His respiratory status improved to baseline, and he was discharged to extended care with instructions to maintain tube care and medication routines.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
